Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase! The players of Bangladesh are out, forming a final huddle, where the skipper Litton Das gives a pep talk before they spread out to take their respective positions. Also, walk out the two openers of Sri Lanka, where Pathum Nissanka will open the innings alongside Kusal Mendis. Also, Shoriful Islam has the new ball in his hands, and he will start the proceedings with a slip in place. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Now, it’s over to Sri Lanka’s batters, and while 140 might not look like a mountain, it can still be a tricky chase under the lights in Abu Dhabi. The ball has been gripping for the spinners, and the Bangladeshi seamers will look to exploit any movement upfront just like the Lankan quicks did earlier. A couple of early wickets could suddenly make this chase interesting, especially with the pressure of a tournament game and the pitch slowing down in the second innings. On the flip side, if Sri Lanka’s experienced top order settles in, they have more than enough firepower to make this chase a stroll. So, will we see another collapse like Bangladesh’s first half, or will Sri Lanka cruise home with authority? The chase is about to begin, so don't go anywhere.

A fightback then. Jaker and Shamim played with patience first and then authority, putting together an unbeaten 86-run stand for the sixth wicket. Shamim looked fluent, while Jaker was solid. The duo picked boundaries at the right moments, especially against Dasun Shanaka and Matheesha Pathirana, whose expensive spells shifted the momentum back. Even though Chameera came back brilliantly at the death with pinpoint yorkers, Bangladesh had done enough to drag themselves to a competitive total. From 53/5 to 139/5, it has been a rescue mission well executed.

Charith Asalanka won the toss and chose to field, and the new-ball bowlers responded with fire. Nuwan Thushara bowled a testing first over, making Tanzid Hasan look like a passenger before rattling his stumps. Dushmantha Chameera followed it up by removing Parvez Hossain Emon, and suddenly, Bangladesh were 0/2 after two consecutive Wicket-Maidens. Tawhid Hridoy’s nervy stay ended with a self-inflicted run-out, Mahedi Hasan was trapped by Wanindu Hasaranga, and when Litton Das fell after scratching around for 28, the scoreboard showed 53/5 inside 10 overs. At that point, Bangladesh looked like they’d struggle to even touch 100.

SCRAPPY AND GRITTY. That was an innings of two halves. Bangladesh stumbled horribly early, losing half their side for just 53, but thanks to a fighting 86-run partnership between Jaker Ali and Shamim Hossain, they clawed their way to 139/5, giving something to their bowlers to bowl. Meanwhile, Sri Lanka’s bowlers were superb for most of the night, yet they’ll feel they let things slip in the middle after such a dominating start.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! Sri Lanka is in full control of the match, having taken five wickets so far, while Bangladesh are feeling the pressure. The Sri Lankan bowlers started off strong, first two overs - WICKET MAIDENS. Since then, the pressure has only increased on the Bangladeshi batters. Wanindu Hasaranga has looked particularly threatening, having taken two wickets and could have had a third if a bail had fallen despite the lights turning on. With skipper Litton Das now back in the dugout, Bangladesh need a miracle to post a respectable total. They are in a desperate situation. With that, Shamim Hossain walks in next to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Wanindu Hasaranga gets his second wicket, and this is a big one in the game's context. Full and on the leg stump line, spinning in back a touch from the deck. Litton Das employs the reverse sweep, but the ball just pops up, and he misses playing the shot. It gets lobbed up, toward the left of the keeper, and Kusal Mendis does the rest with a simple grab. A huge appeal for caught behind now, but the umpire stays unmoved. The Lankans think they have got their man, and this is sent upstairs for a review. Now, the question is whether the ball clipped the left glove of the batter. And even before the technology comes up, Litton Das starts to march back. Finally, the UltraEdge is here and shows a clear spike and the on-field decision is overturned. Litton Das departs for 28 (26), and Bangladesh are 53/5.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with 'Sri Lanka Matha' and 'Amar Shonar Bangla', and all other pre-match formalities. No doubt, this growing rivalry between these two nations has been a giant crowd-puller. We can see that in the stands as fans have flocked in large numbers to support their beloved sides. It is time to get going in Match number 5 at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi. The umpires make their way to the middle. Charith Asalanka leads his men out of the brief huddle talk, as the Lankans scatter across the field to take their positions. Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan walk out to open for Bangladesh. And it will be the slingy pacer, Nuwan Thushara, to bowl the first over of the game. Will he get some swing first up? Hasan to face. Here we go...

The stage is set, but before the action, it's time for the national anthems, with the match officials and players from both sides lined up. A moment of honour and respect before the battle begins. It will be Sri Lanka's first, followed by Bangladesh's.

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan is pitchside for his analysis. Informs that it is a fresh pitch with a tinge of grass. Reckons that the ball will skid a little, and the length ball will be a bit difficult for the batters to hit through the line. Opines that chasing might be a better option on this track. Matt Floyd joins in and says that it is a bit breezy and points out that it will be better if the batters try and hit into the wind. Bazid further mentions that it might quicken up a bit as the game progresses.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kamil Mishara, Kusal Perera, Charith Asalanka (C), Dasun Shanaka, Kamindu Mendis, Wanindu Hasaranga, Dushmantha Chameera, Matheesha Pathirana, and Nuwan Thushara.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Parvez Hossain Emon, Tanzid Hasan, Litton Das (C/WK), Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Shoriful Islam (In place of Taskin Ahmed), and Mustafizur Rahman.

The skipper of Bangladesh, Litton Das, says that they don’t mind batting first as the wicket looks good. Reflecting on the first game, he mentions that while Bangladesh played good cricket, there are still areas that need improvement. To win matches, he stresses, every aspect has to click together. Informs that Taskin Ahmed misses out, with Shoriful Islam coming into the XI.

The captain of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, says it looks like a fresh pitch, and hence, that is the reason behind bowling first. Adds that they are looking to keep the momentum going, being the defending champions of the T20I format. Informs that Wanindu Hasaranga is fit and back in the side, and also shares that they are going with a 7-4 combination, with three all-rounders.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Sri Lanka, and the skipper, Charith Asalanka, has elected to FIELD first.

So, what can we expect today? A battle of fine margins. Sri Lanka’s pedigree against Bangladesh’s new aggressive blueprint makes this a must-watch. Head-to-head overall, the numbers tilt slightly Sri Lanka’s way with 12 wins to Bangladesh’s 8, but in recent times, the Tigers have struck back strongly, including a 2-1 series win in Sri Lanka just this July. Group B is unforgiving, with Afghanistan also in the mix, so the loser here will be staring at a tough road to qualification. Expect spin to play a role on the Abu Dhabi pitch, with names like Hasaranga and Rishad to shoulder responsibility. With all of that, stay tuned for the toss and team lineups!

On the flip side, we have Bangladesh. What’s their edge? Momentum and a new mindset. Under power-hitting coach Julian Wood, Bangladesh are gearing their approach for next year’s T20I World Cup, and the signs are already showing. In their opening game against Hong Kong, China, Litton Das played a captain’s knock of 59 off 39, supported by Tawhid Hridoy, as they chased 144 with ease. Taskin Ahmed and Tanzim Hasan Sakib picked up two wickets each, while leg-spinner Rishad Hossain once again proved why he’s becoming a key figure. They ticked most of the boxes in their first match, but the question, however, is whether they can bring the same intent against stronger attacks.

Let’s know a bit about the lions first. What does Sri Lanka need from this match? A confident start and a settled combination. The Charith Asalanka-led side warmed up with a 2-1 series victory over Zimbabwe, but the scars of inconsistency still linger, as their collapse to 80 all out in one of those matches is fresh in memory. The return of Wanindu Hasaranga, fit again after a hamstring injury, is a massive boost, giving them a proven match-winner with both bat and ball. Pathum Nissanka has been in sublime T20I form this year, and his Powerplay runs will be crucial. But can the bowlers click together? That remains the question. With Dushmantha Chameera and Nuwan Thushara likely to take the new ball, supported by Hasaranga’s guile, Sri Lanka will need balance to stay alive in this group where every slip could be fatal.

THE TIGERS vs THE LIONS! Are you up for a growing modern-day Asian rivalry that has produced drama, heated moments, and unforgettable contests? But one can ask, why does this clash feel different from the others in the Asia Cup 2025? Because when Sri Lanka and Bangladesh meet, it’s not just about cricket. Now, in the ‘Group of Death’ of this Asia Cup, where every point matters, the opening battle between these two could shape the road to qualification. Sri Lanka, six-time champions, begin their campaign at the Zayed Cricket Stadium, while Bangladesh already have two points on the board. On that note, you are welcome to our coverage of the fifth match.
... MATCH DAY ...

A new chapter is set to unfold in a rivalry that has grown increasingly fiery in recent years as Bangladesh and Sri Lanka face off at the Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi. Group B has long been billed as the 'group of death' with Sri Lanka, Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Hong Kong, China all competing for just two Super Four spots. The stakes are high, and two points from this clash could prove decisive in shaping the qualification race. While Sri Lanka are yet to begin their campaign, Bangladesh already have a win under their belt, albeit a hard-fought one against Hong Kong, China. The Litton Das-led side were favourites and ultimately secured the points, but not without being tested. Hong Kong, China were restricted to 143 with Taskin Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib and Rishad Hossain among the wickets, although the overall bowling effort left room for improvement, particularly at the death. In the chase, Litton Das and Towhid Hridoy steadied the innings after a brisk start. Boundaries were hard to come by in the middle overs, so the duo kept the scoreboard ticking with busy running between the wickets. That approach could become the blueprint for Bangladesh’s batting unit on surfaces where big shots are difficult to clear. Sri Lanka, champions of the last T20I edition of the Asia Cup in 2022, have not had the smoothest build-up. They lost a home T20I series to Bangladesh in July and were pushed hard in Zimbabwe more recently. However, the return of Wanindu Hasaranga from a hamstring injury is a massive boost, not only with the ball but also as part of a strong pool of all-rounders that includes Dasun Shanaka, Chamika Karunaratne and Janith Liyanage. Pathum Nissanka has shouldered much of the batting burden this year, but Sri Lanka will need Kusal Perera, Kusal Mendis, Charith Asalanka and Kamindu Mendis to find form if they are to go deep into the tournament. On the bowling front, Dushmantha Chameera has made a strong return to the T20I setup through the Zimbabwe series and will aim to carry that rhythm into this tournament. He is expected to spearhead the attack, with Nuwan Thushara, Binura Fernando and Matheesha Pathirana providing the support cast. Maheesh Theekshana has not quite hit the heights he is known for this year, and Sri Lanka will hope he rediscovers his best form on the big stage. As Bangladesh look to build on their opening win and Sri Lanka begin their campaign with renewed confidence, who are you backing to come out on top in this high-stakes Group B clash?
